_meta.method: complete direct literal rendering; source order preserved; no explanatory paraphrase

word_for_word: चित्ते शुद्धेऽपि न ध्यानं विना संन्यासमात्रतः मुक्तिः स्यादिति षष्ठेऽस्मिन्ध्यानयोगो वितन्यते
even when the mind is purified, liberation does not arise merely from renunciation without meditation; therefore in this sixth chapter the yoga of meditation is expounded
पूर्वाध्यायान्ते संक्षेपेणोक्तं योगं प्रपञ्चयितुं षष्ठाध्यायारम्भः
the sixth chapter begins in order to elaborate the yoga briefly stated at the end of the previous chapter
सर्वकर्माणि मनसा इत्यारभ्य संन्यासपूर्विकाया ज्ञाननिष्ठायास्तात्पर्येणाभिधानात् दुःखस्वरूपत्वाच्च कर्मणः सहसा संन्यासातिप्रसङ्गं प्राप्तं वारयितुं संन्यासादपि श्रेष्ठत्वेन कर्मयोगं स्तौति

because steadfastness in knowledge preceded by renunciation was chiefly taught beginning with ‘all actions mentally,’ and because action is painful, there is danger of premature renunciation; to prevent this he praises karma-yoga as superior even to renunciation
श्रीभगवानुवाच अनाश्रित इति द्वाभ्याम्
the Blessed Lord said in two verses beginning ‘not depending’
कर्मफलमनाश्रितोऽनपेक्षमाणः अवश्यं कर्तव्यतया विहितं कर्म यः करोति स एव संन्यासी योगी च
one who performs action enjoined as necessarily to be done without depending on or expecting its fruit is himself a renouncer and yogin
नतु निरग्निः अग्निसाध्येष्टाख्यकर्मत्यागी न चाक्रियोऽनग्निसाध्यपूर्ताख्यकर्मत्यागी च
not merely one without fire who abandons sacrificial actions dependent on fire, nor one without activity who abandons public works not dependent on fire
कुत इत्यपेक्षायां कर्मयोगस्यैव संन्यासत्वं संपादयन्नाह यमिति
when asked why, he establishes karma-yoga itself as renunciation with ‘what they call renunciation’
यं संन्यासमिति प्राहुः प्रकर्षेण श्रेष्ठत्वेनाहुः संन्यास एवात्यरेचयत् इत्यादिश्रुतेः
that which they call renunciation, praised as especially superior in Śruti such as ‘renunciation alone surpassed’
केवलात्फलसंन्यसनाद्धेतोः योगमेव तं जानीहि
know that very yoga to be renunciation because it consists simply in renouncing fruit
न संन्यस्तः फलसंकल्पो येन सः कर्मनिष्ठो ज्ञाननिष्ठो वा कश्चिदपि न हि योगी भवति
no one established in action or knowledge becomes a yogin unless intention toward fruit has been renounced
अतः फलसंकल्पत्यागसाम्यात्संन्यासात्संन्यासी च फलसंकल्पत्यागादेव चित्तविक्षेपाभावाद्योगी च भवत्येव स इत्यर्थः
therefore through the common feature of abandoning intention toward fruit he is a renouncer, and because that very abandonment removes distraction of mind he is also a yogin; this is the meaning
तर्हि यावज्जीवं कर्मयोग एव प्राप्त इत्याशङ्क्य तस्यावधिमाह आरुरुक्षोरिति
objection: then karma-yoga would continue for life; he states its limit with ‘for one wishing to ascend’
ज्ञानयोगमारोढुं प्राप्तुमिच्छोः पुंसस्तदारोहे कारणं कर्मोच्यते चित्तशुद्धिकरत्वात्
for a person wishing to ascend to jñāna-yoga, action is said to be the cause of ascent because it purifies the mind
ज्ञानयोगमारूढस्य तु तस्यैव ज्ञाननिष्ठस्य शमः समाधिश्चित्तविक्षेपकर्मोपरमो ज्ञानपरिपाके कारणमुच्यते
but for one who has ascended to jñāna-yoga and is established in knowledge, tranquility—samādhi and cessation of actions that distract the mind—is said to cause maturation of knowledge
कीदृशोऽसौ योगारूढः यस्य शमः कारणमुच्यत इत्यत्राह यदा हीति
what is one established in yoga, for whom tranquility is said to be the cause? he says this with ‘when indeed’
इन्द्रियार्थेषु इन्द्रियभोग्येषु शब्दादिषु तत्साधनेषु च कर्मसु यदा नानुषज्जते आसक्तिं न करोति
when he does not cling to or become attached to sense objects such as sound or to actions that are means for obtaining them
तत्र हेतुः आसक्तिमूलभूतान्सर्वान्भोगविषयान्कर्मविषयांश्च संकल्पान्संन्यसितुं त्यक्तुं शीलं यस्य सः
the reason: he is disposed to renounce, abandon, all conceptions concerning enjoyments and actions that form the root of attachment
तदा योगारूढ उच्यते
then he is called established in yoga
अतो विषयासक्तित्यागे मोक्षं तदासक्तौ च बन्धं पर्यालोच्य रागादिस्वभावं त्यजेदित्याह उद्धरेदिति

therefore, considering liberation to lie in abandonment of attachment to objects and bondage in attachment to them, one should abandon the nature of attachment and the rest; he says this with ‘one should raise’
आत्मना विवेकयुक्तेनात्मानं संसारादुद्धरेन्नत्ववसादयेदधो न नयेत्
by the self endowed with discrimination one should raise oneself from saṃsāra and not depress oneself or lead oneself downward
हि यस्मादात्मैव मनः सङ्गादुपरत आत्मनः स्वस्य बन्धुरुपकारकः रिपुरपकारकश्च
for the self, the mind, when withdrawn from attachment is one’s own friend and benefactor, and when attached is one’s enemy and injurer
कथंभूतस्यात्मैव बन्धुः कथंभूतस्य चात्मैव रिपुरित्यपेक्षायामाह बन्धुरिति
for what kind of person is the self friend and for what kind enemy? he says ‘friend’
येनात्मनैवात्मा कार्यकारणसंघातरूपो जितो वशीकृतस्तस्य तथाभूतस्यात्मन आत्मैव बन्धुः
for one by whom the lower self, the aggregate of effect and cause, has been conquered and controlled by the self itself, that self is his friend
अनात्मनोऽजितात्मनस्त्वात्मैवात्मनः शत्रुत्वे शत्रुवदपकारकारित्वे वर्तेत
but for one who has not mastered himself, the self acts toward himself as an enemy, causing harm like an enemy
जितात्मनः स्वस्मिन्बन्धुत्वं स्फुटयति जितात्मन इति
he makes clear how the self is a friend to one who has conquered himself, with ‘of one who has conquered the self’
जित आत्मा येन तस्य प्रशान्तस्य रागादिरहितस्यैव परं केवलमात्मा शीतोष्णादिषु सत्स्वपि समाहितः स्वात्मनिष्ठो भवति नान्यस्य

for one who has conquered the self and is tranquil, free from attachment and the like, the supreme Self alone remains composed and established in itself even amid heat, cold, and the like; not for another
यद्वा तस्य हृदि परमात्मा समाहितः स्थितो भवति
or, the Supreme Self is established in his heart
योगारूढस्य लक्षणं श्रैष्ठ्यं चोक्तमुपपाद्योपसंहरति ज्ञानविज्ञानतृप्तात्मेति
having explained the characteristics and superiority of one established in yoga, he concludes with ‘satisfied by knowledge and realization’
ज्ञानमौपदेशिकं विज्ञानमपरोक्षानुभवः ताभ्यां तृप्तो निराकाङ्क्ष आत्मा चित्तं यस्य
jñāna is instructional knowledge and vijñāna direct experience; one whose self, mind, is satisfied by these and without expectation
अतः कूटस्थो निर्विकारः
therefore he is kūṭastha, changeless
अतएव विजितानीन्द्रियाणि येन
and therefore his senses are conquered
अतएव समानि लोष्टादीनि यस्य मृत्खण्डपाषाणसुवर्णेषु हेयोपादेयबुद्धिशून्यः
and therefore earth-clod, stone, and gold are equal for him, free from the cognition ‘to be rejected’ and ‘to be acquired’
स युक्तो योगारूढ इत्युच्यते
he is called disciplined, established in yoga
सुहृन्मित्रादिषु समबुद्धियुक्तस्ततोऽपि श्रेष्ठ इत्याह सुहृदिति
one whose understanding is equal toward well-wishers, friends, and the rest is still superior; he says this with ‘well-wisher’
सुहृत् स्वभावेनैव हिताशंसी
a well-wisher naturally desires one’s welfare
मित्रं स्नेहवशेनोपकारकः
a friend helps through affection
अरिर्घातुकः
an enemy seeks to harm
उदासीनो विवदमानयोरुभयोरप्युपेक्षकः
a neutral person is indifferent to both parties in a dispute
मध्यस्थो विवदमानयोरपि हिताशंसी
a mediator desires the welfare of both disputants
द्वेष्यो द्वेषविषयः
one hated is an object of aversion
बन्धुः संबन्धी
a relative is one connected by relation
साधवः सदाचाराः पापा दुराचाराः
the good are well-conducted; sinners are ill-conducted
एतेषु समा रागद्वेषादिशून्या बुद्धिर्यस्य स तु विशिष्टः
one whose understanding toward all these is equal and free from attachment and aversion is distinguished
एवं योगारूढस्य लक्षणमुक्त्वेदानीं तस्य साङ्गं योगं विधत्ते योगीत्यादिना स योगी परमो मत इत्यन्तेन ग्रन्थेन
having stated the characteristics of one established in yoga, he now prescribes yoga together with its limbs in the passage from ‘the yogin’ through ‘that yogin is considered supreme’
योगी योगारूढः आत्मानं मनो युञ्जीत समाहितं कुर्यात्
the yogin established in yoga should yoke the self, the mind, make it composed
सततं निरन्तरं रहस्येकान्ते स्थितः सन्
constantly, without interruption, staying in a secret solitary place
एकाकी सङ्गशून्यः
alone, without association
यतं संयतं चित्तमात्मा देहश्च यस्य
with mind and body restrained
निराशीर्निराकाङ्क्षो निराहारो वा
without expectation or, alternatively, fasting
अपरिग्रहः परिग्रहशून्यश्च
without possessions
आसननियमं दर्शयन्नाह शुचाविति द्वाभ्याम्
showing the rule for the seat, he speaks in two verses beginning ‘in a clean place’
शुद्धे स्थाने आत्मनः स्वस्यासनं स्थापयित्वा
having established one’s own seat in a clean place
कीदृशम् स्थिरमचलम् नातिचोन्नतं न चातिनीचं च
what kind? firm, unmoving, neither too high nor too low
चैलं वस्त्रमजिनं व्याघ्रादिचर्म चैलाजिने कुशेभ्य उत्तरे यस्मिन्
cloth and animal skin such as tiger skin are above the kuśa grass
कुशानामुपरि चर्म तदुपरि वस्त्रमास्तीर्येत्यर्थः
spread skin over kuśa grass and cloth over that; this is the meaning
तत्रेति
with ‘there’
तत्र तस्मिन्नासने उपविश्य
sitting there on that seat
एकाग्रं विक्षेपरहितं मनः कृत्वा
making the mind one-pointed, free from distraction
योगं युञ्ज्यादभ्यसेत्
one should practice yoga
यताः संयताश्चित्तस्येन्द्रियाणां च क्रिया यस्य
one whose activities of mind and senses are restrained
आत्मनो मनसो विशुद्धये उपशान्तये
for purification and tranquility of the self, the mind
